docs.title: ✨ What is FixMyMedTech?
docs.text:
A platform that gives biomedical engineers the knowledge, tools, and community to diagnose, repair, and maintain medical equipment — anywhere on the continent.

Fix My MedTech is an open-source platform where biomedical engineers tag, track, diagnose, and repair medical devices. It is built around the realities of the field: devices that arrive without manuals, without spare parts, and often already degraded — in environments where heat, humidity, dust and unstable power accelerate failure far beyond what manufacturers expect.

docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  • The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
  • Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at hello@careagain.org. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: 4. Permanent Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.text:

For answers to common questions about this code of conduct, see the FAQ at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq. Translations are available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/translations.

docs.title: FixMyMedTech — Architecture Guide
docs.text:
Medical equipment management platform for LMICs (Low and Middle Income Countries).

Stack: FastAPI (REST backend) + FastHTML (frontend) + Supabase (database & auth)

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text:
Browser
  │
  ▼
FastHTML (port 5000)          ← renders HTML pages, handles sessions
  │  httpx async requests
  ▼
FastAPI (port 8000)           ← REST API, business logic, auth validation
  │  supabase-py
  ▼
Supabase (PostgreSQL)         ← database, auth, file storage

FastHTML is not a traditional frontend — it is a Python web server that generates HTML server-side. There is no JavaScript framework, no build step, and no API calls from the browser. The browser talks only to FastHTML. FastHTML talks to FastAPI. FastAPI talks to Supabase.

Authentication uses Supabase JWT tokens stored in server-side sessions (cookies). The token never touches the browser directly.

docs.title: Project structure
docs.text:
fixmymedtech/
│
├── backend/                        ← FastAPI REST API
│   ├── main.py                     ← App entry point, CORS, router registration
│   ├── deps.py                     ← Auth helpers, get_current_user
│   ├── requirements.txt
│   ├── .env.example
│   └── routers/
│       ├── auth.py                 ← POST /api/auth/login, /signup, /logout
│       ├── devices.py              ← CRUD /api/devices + public QR endpoint
│       ├── fault_reports.py        ← Fault submission and management
│       └── dashboard.py            ← Aggregated stats
│
├── frontend/                       ← FastHTML frontend server
│   ├── main.py                     ← All routes and page rendering
│   ├── api.py                      ← HTTP client (calls FastAPI via httpx)
│   ├── components.py               ← Reusable UI components, page shells
│   ├── requirements.txt
│   ├── .env.example
│   └── static/
│       ├── styles.css              ← All CSS — edit this to change the design
│       └── *.png / *.svg           ← Images and icons
│
├── docs/                           ← MkDocs documentation
│   ├── mkdocs.yml
│   └── docs/*.md
│
└── docker-compose.yml              ← Runs all services together

docs.title: Why two servers?
docs.text:
FastHTML handles routing and rendering. FastAPI handles data and business logic. This separation means:

  • The API can be used independently by mobile apps or third parties later
  • Backend logic stays in FastAPI where it is easier to test
  • FastHTML stays thin — it only fetches data and renders HTML

docs.title: Why server-side sessions?
docs.text: JWT tokens are stored in encrypted server-side sessions (cookies), not in localStorage or the browser. This is more secure — the token is never exposed to JavaScript or visible in the browser.

docs.title: Why Supabase?
docs.text: Supabase provides PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, and row-level security in one managed service. Row Level Security (RLS) ensures each hospital can only see its own devices and data, enforced at the database level.

docs.title: User roles
docs.text: Role What they can do clinical_staff Scan QR codes, view device info, report faults technician All of the above + update device status, log maintenance admin All of the above + create/delete devices, manage users

docs.title: Page map
docs.text: URL Auth Who What /login No Anyone Sign in /signup No Anyone Create account /dashboard Yes Admin / Technician Stats overview /devices Yes Admin / Technician Device list with filters /devices/new Yes Admin / Technician Register new device /devices/{id} Yes Admin / Technician Device detail, history, faults /d/{id} No Anyone with QR Public device page /d/{id}/report No Anyone with QR Submit fault report

docs.title: Data flow — QR scan (no login)
docs.text:
1. Nurse scans QR on device
2. Browser opens: https://yourdomain.com/d/{device_id}
3. FastHTML calls: GET {API_URL}/api/devices/public/{device_id}
4. FastAPI queries Supabase (no auth required for this endpoint)
5. FastHTML renders device info, manuals, fault report form
6. Nurse submits fault → FastHTML calls POST /api/faults/public
7. FastAPI updates Supabase, device status changes to "fault" if critical

docs.title: Data flow — admin login
docs.text:
1. Admin submits login form
2. FastHTML calls: POST {API_URL}/api/auth/login
3. FastAPI calls Supabase Auth → gets JWT token
4. FastHTML stores token in encrypted session cookie
5. All subsequent requests include token in Authorization header (server-side)
6. FastAPI validates token on every protected endpoint via Depends(get_current_user)

docs.title: 1. Supabase
docs.text:
1. Create a project at https://supabase.com
  2. The schema is applied automatically: backend startup runs the migrations in infrastructure/migrations/ (tracked in fixmymedtech.schema_migrations).
  3. Go to Project Settings → API → copy your keys

docs.title: 2. Backend (FastAPI)
docs.text:
cd backend
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env:
# DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://postgres:xxx@db.your-project.supabase.co:5432/postgres
# DB_SCHEMA=fixmymedtech
# FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:8888

pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8888

# API runs at:  {API_URL}
# Swagger docs: {API_URL}/docs

docs.title: 3. Frontend (FastHTML)
docs.text:
cd frontend
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env:
# API_URL=http://localhost:8888
# SESSION_SECRET=any-random-string

pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py

# App runs at: http://localhost:5000

docs.title: 4. Documentation (MkDocs)
docs.text:
cd docs
pip install mkdocs-material
mkdocs serve

# Docs at: http://localhost:8080

docs.title: With Docker Compose (recommended)
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
# Fill in all values

docker compose up --build -d

Services will be available at:

Service URL Frontend (FastHTML) Backend (FastAPI) API docs Documentation

docs.title: Backend (backend/.env)
docs.text: Variable Description DATABASE_URL PostgreSQL connection string (asyncpg driver) DB_SCHEMA Schema the app tables live in (e.g. fixmymedtech) FRONTEND_URL Backend URL used for email links + redirects (e.g. http://localhost:8888)

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
No .env file is needed — both variables have working defaults:

Variable Description API_URL FastAPI URL (default http://localhost:8888) SESSION_SECRET Random string for encrypting session cookies (default dev-secret-change-in-production)

docs.title: QR codes
docs.text:
Each device gets a permanent public URL:

https://yourdomain.com/d/{device_id}

The UUID never changes. The content behind it updates in the database. To generate a printable QR label:

  1. Go to https://qr.io or https://www.qrcode-monkey.com
  2. Enter the device URL
  3. Download as SVG or PNG
  4. Print on water-resistant label and attach to device

docs.title: Authentication Guide
docs.text:
This guide describes every authentication & account lifecycle flow in FixMyMedTech: self signup, email verification, login/logout, password reset, admin-invited users, admin portal access, and social (OAuth2) login.

Stack: FastAPI + FastAPI-Users (auth core) · FastHTML (frontend) · Authlib (social login) · SQLAdmin (admin portal) · Postgres

docs.title: 1. Identity model
docs.text:
Accounts live in the local fixmymedtech.users table (Postgres). The core auth machinery is provided by FastAPI-Users 15 (backend/config/users.py), which we hide behind the app's own router (backend/routers/auth.py) so the browser-facing API contract stays stable.

Key fields on users:

Field Meaning email Unique login id (always stored lower-case) hashed_password bcrypt password hash (via pwdlib/BcryptHasher) is_active Disabled accounts can't log in is_verified Email verified (login does not enforce this) is_superuser Grants access to the /admin portal

The 1:1 profile, default organization and membership are created alongside a new user by every provisioning path (signup, OAuth, admin invite).

docs.title: 2. Tokens & sessions
docs.text: All tokens are JWTs signed with AUTH_JWT_SECRET (≥ 32 bytes, HS256).

docs.title: Login token
docs.text: Minted by the JWT auth backend (JWTStrategy, lifetime AUTH_TOKEN_TTL, default 7 days), payload {sub, exp}. It is a Bearer token: the frontend ships it to the backend as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

docs.title: Server-side session (frontend)
docs.text:
The FastHTML frontend stores the login token server-side in an encrypted cookie session, never in localStorage:

  • /login POST → req.session["token"] = access_token
  • features/auth/helper.py → get_token(req), clear_session(req), require_auth() / require_auth_verified() (validates against /api/dashboard/stats and redirects to /login?expired=1 on 401)
  • /logout clears the session (the backend JWT is stateless)

So the browser only ever holds the session cookie; the JWT never reaches it.

docs.title: Email tokens (verification / reset / invitation)
docs.text:
These are signed with the same AUTH_JWT_SECRET but have a different payload shape and are consumed by FastAPI-Users' verify() / reset_password() UserManager methods:

Token Claims aud TTL Login {sub, exp} fastapi-users:auth 7 d Verify email {sub, email, exp} fastapi-users:verify 1 h Reset password {sub, email, password_fgpt, exp} fastapi-users:reset 1 h

password_fgpt is required. reset_password() verifies password_fgpt (a bcrypt hash of the user's current hashed_password) against that stored hash. Any hand-minted reset token missing this claim is rejected with HTTP 400 Reset failed:. Never build these tokens by hand — route them through UserManager.forgot_password() or reproduce the exact claim set described in §6.

docs.title: 3. Self signup (public)
docs.text:
browser → POST /api/auth/signup {email, password, full_name, organization_id?, ...}
  1. UserManager.create() hashes the password (bcrypt), is_verified=false
  2. Profile row created (id = user id, generated username)
  3. Organization resolved-or-created + OrgUser membership (role)
  4. on_after_register hook sends a WELCOME email + a VERIFICATION email

Response is {message}. Duplicate email → HTTP 409 user_already_exists. The frontend /signup page renders distinct success / "account already exists" states.

A self-registered user is is_verified=false but can log in immediately (login does not gate on verification).

docs.title: 4. Email verification
docs.text:
Triggered on self signup (on_after_register) or on demand via POST /api/auth/request-verification (anti-enumeration: always returns the same message).

  1. The hook calls UserManager.request_verify() → verification token {sub, email, aud: fastapi-users:verify} (1 h).
  2. send_verification_email() builds a backend link {API_BASE_URL}/api/auth/verify?token=... — note it points at FastAPI, because /api/auth/* is a backend route.
  3. user_manager.verify(token, request) checks signature + audience, that sub/email match the stored user, and sets is_verified = true.
  4. The router then 302s the browser to {FRONTEND_URL}/login?verified=1 (or ?verified=0 on failure), and the login page shows a corresponding alert.

Template: backend/templates/email_verification.html.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
POST /api/auth/login {email, password}
  • get_by_email (lower-cased)      → 404 user_not_found
  • verify_and_update(bcrypt)       → 401 invalid_credentials
  • hash-rotation (argon2→bcrypt)   → transparent upgrade
  • JWTStrategy.write_token(user)   → {access_token, user:{id, email}}

The frontend /login POST stores the token in the session and redirects to /dashboard (or ?next=). Error mapping shown to the user: user_not_found / email_not_confirmed / invalid_credentials.

docs.title: Logout
docs.text: POST /api/auth/logout returns {message} — it is stateless; the frontend /logout route just clears the server-side session and redirects to /login.

docs.title: 6. Password reset ("Forgot password")
docs.text:
Public flow, fully functional since the reset-token fix:

POST /api/auth/forgot-password {email}      (body: LoginRequest incl. password)
  → UserManager.forgot_password()
      token = {sub, password_fgpt = bcrypt(current hashed_password),
               aud: fastapi-users:reset}   (1 h)
  → on_after_forgot_password → send_reset_password_email()
      link = {FRONTEND_URL}/reset-password?token=...     (frontend page)
  → always returns the same message (no email-address disclosure)

The invited user clicks the link → FastHTML /reset-password?token=...:

GET  /reset-password?token=…   renders the form (redirects to /login if absent)
POST /reset-password {token, password, password2}
      validates: token present, len ≥ 8, passwords match
      → POST /api/auth/reset-password?token=…&password=…   (query params!)
          → UserManager.reset_password(token, password)
              verifies signature + aud + password_fgpt vs current hash
              400 Reset failed: … on bad/expired/single-use token
      success screen → "Go to login"

Important details:

  • The backend endpoint declares token and password as query parameters, so the frontend API helper (_post) appends them to the URL and sends an empty JSON body.
  • Reset tokens are single-use and the fingerprint ties them to the exact current hash — changing the password invalidates any outstanding link.
  • Template: backend/templates/email_reset_password.html.

docs.title: 7. Admin-invited user (invitation email)
docs.text:
When a superuser creates a user in the SQLAdmin portal (/admin/user/create), UserAdmin provisions a fully-functional account and sends an invitation email — not a verification email:

  1. on_model_change normalizes/strips fields, forces is_verified=false, seeds a random password hash.
  2. after_model_change creates the Profile, a default Organization and an OrgUser (role admin).
  3. It mints a proper reset token (same shape as §6 {sub, email, password_fgpt, aud: fastapi-users:reset}, 1 h) and sends send_invitation_email() → backend/templates/email_invitation.html ("You've been invited to FixMyMedTech", button links to {FRONTEND_URL}/reset-password?token=...).
  4. The invited user sets their own password through the reset page and can then log in (login doesn't require verification).

A mail failure is logged and never aborts user creation.

Gotcha (fixed): the old tokens used aud: fastapi-users:reset-password and omitted password_fgpt, so every such link returned 400 Reset failed:. The invitation route must use aud: fastapi-users:reset and include the fingerprint claim to be accepted by reset_password().

docs.title: Admin-side email actions (backend/routers/admin_email.py, /admin-panel)
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose GET /admin-panel/invite Invitation form (full_name, email) POST /admin-panel/invite Find-or-create user, sends verification email POST /admin-panel/send-verification/{user_id} Resend verification link POST /admin-panel/send-reset/{user_id} Reset-password email (with password_fgpt)

All require the admin session (require_superuser).

docs.title: 8. Admin portal (/admin)
docs.text:
The SQLAdmin UI at /admin is guarded by AdminAuth (backend/admin_auth.py):

  • Login is a form POST (username = email, password), validated with pwdlib against the stored bcrypt hash and is_active + is_superuser.
  • On success the session cookie stores admin_user_id (signed with AUTH_SESSION_SECRET).
  • Every request re-verifies that the id maps to an active superuser (authenticate()).
  • require_superuser() is the FastAPI dependency equivalent for the /admin-panel/* endpoints (HTTP 403 otherwise).

Create a superuser with docker compose exec backend python scripts/create_superuser.py (or promote an existing user's is_superuser flag).

docs.title: 9. Social login (OAuth2)
docs.text:
Optional providers — Google, GitHub, Discord — registered in backend/config/oauth.py from *_CLIENT_ID / *_CLIENT_SECRET env vars (only when both are set).

browser → GET /api/auth/oauth/{provider}            (frontend /login buttons)
  → Authlib redirects to the provider
provider → GET /api/auth/oauth/{provider}/callback
  1. exchange code for access token
  2. fetch userinfo (email + name)
  3. find-or-create LOCAL users row (upsert)
       • new user: hashed_password="!" (unusable), is_verified=true
       • profile + default org + admin membership created
  4. mint a LOCAL JWT (JWTStrategy) and redirect to
     {FRONTEND_URL}/oauth-callback?access_token=…
     (token passes through the URL for a single hop)
frontend → /oauth-callback stores token in the session → /dashboard

Notes:

  • Discord only returns email when the identify email scopes apply and the account has a verified email; the code then falls back to discord-{id}@fixmymedtech.local (flagged so admins can fix it).
  • GitHub uses the user:email scope; profile name is name/preferred_username.
  • The OAuth user can later log in with !-hash accounts only through OAuth — use admin send-reset to give them a password if needed.

docs.title: 10. Endpoint reference
docs.text: Method Path Auth Purpose POST /api/auth/signup – Self registration POST /api/auth/login – Password login POST /api/auth/logout – Stateless logout GET /api/auth/me JWT Profile + organizations PATCH /api/auth/me JWT Update full_name / username GET /api/auth/tasks JWT My faults + maintenance tasks GET /api/auth/verify – Verify ?token= (redirects) POST /api/auth/request-verification – Resend verification email POST /api/auth/forgot-password – Send reset link POST /api/auth/reset-password – ?token=&password= set new pwd GET /api/auth/oauth/{provider} – Start OAuth GET /api/auth/oauth/{provider}/callback – OAuth callback GET/POST /login, /signup, /reset-password – FastHTML pages GET /oauth-callback, /logout sess FastHTML session helpers POST /admin/login, /admin/logout – SQLAdmin portal GET/POST /admin/* admin SQLAdmin portal UI POST /admin-panel/invite admin Invite user + verification email POST /admin-panel/send-verification/{id} admin Resend verification POST /admin-panel/send-reset/{id} admin Send reset-password email

docs.title: 11. Email templates & triggers
docs.text:
Template Trigger Link → email_welcome (inline in config.email) Self signup on_after_register – email_verification.html Self signup / request-verification /api/auth/verify email_reset_password.html forgot-password (+ admin send-reset) /reset-password email_invitation.html Admin-created user (UserAdmin.after_model_change) /reset-password

All render with {logo_url} (from LOGO_URL) and {link}. When MAIL_SERVER is unset, send_message() logs the email to the backend console instead of sending (local dev).

docs.title: 12. Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Used for Default AUTH_JWT_SECRET Signs login / verify / reset JWTs (≥ 32 bytes) old 30-byte dev secret AUTH_TOKEN_TTL Login JWT lifetime (seconds) 604800 (7 d) AUTH_SESSION_SECRET Admin portal session cookie dev-admin-session-secret FRONTEND_URL Base for reset/invite links & OAuth callback http://localhost:8888 API_BASE_URL Base for verify links (backend) http://localhost:8888 PUBLIC_API_URL Overrides API_BASE_URL for verification links – LOGO_URL Branding in email templates Supabase asset URL MAIL_* SMTP (server/port/user/pass/from/starttls/tls) unset → console log GOOGLE_/GITHUB_/DISCORD_CLIENT_* OAuth provider creds unset → provider disabled

docs.title: 13. Security notes
docs.text:
• Emails are lower-cased on input, so User@X.org and user@x.org are the same account.
  • Forgot-password / verification-resend endpoints return a fixed message (no account enumeration).
  • Reset and verification tokens are short-lived (1 h) and signed with the app secret — rotation of AUTH_JWT_SECRET invalidates all outstanding links.
  • Session cookies are HttpOnly server-side sessions; the JWT never reaches the browser.
  • Admin portal and /admin-panel/* are restricted to active superusers.
  • AUTH_JWT_SECRET must be ≥ 32 bytes to avoid the InsecureKeyLengthWarning (generate with openssl rand -base64 48).

docs.title: Collaborating on FixMyMedTech
docs.text:
FixMyMedTech is open source. Everyone is welcome to help: fixing bugs, adding features, improving translations, writing documentation, or testing on real hospital equipment.

The project lives at https://github.com/FixMyMedTech/fixmymedtech-app.

docs.title: 1. Reporting an issue
docs.text: All work is tracked with GitHub Issues. Open one at https://github.com/FixMyMedTech/fixmymedtech-app/issues/new.

docs.title: Before you open an issue
docs.text:
• Search the existing issues (open and closed) — your problem may already have an answer.
  • Use the applicable issue type (Bug report / Feature request / Question).

docs.title: Good bug reports include
docs.text:
• What you did — step-by-step reproduction.
  • What you expected vs. what happened.
  • Environment — browser/device, and which deployment (production platform.fixmymedtech.org or development dev.fixmymedtech.org).
  • Screenshots or a screen recording — a picture is worth 1000 words.
  • Any log output (browser console or docker compose logs backend).

docs.title: Good feature requests include
docs.text:
• The problem you are trying to solve, not just the solution you imagine.
  • Who it helps and why.
  • A rough proposal or mock-up if you have one.

Labels like bug, feature, documentation, good first issue help maintainers triage. If you are not sure where something belongs, just open the issue — we can always relabel it.

docs.title: 2. The collaboration flow
docs.text: Contributions go through the classic fork-and-PR flow. The screenshot below is the summary path we use:

docs.title: Where to branch from
docs.text:
• Development work targets the dev branch. Pushing to dev auto-deploys to the development server (dev.fixmymedtech.org).
  • main auto-deploys to production, so a maintainer merges approved PRs into main — do not push straight to it.
  • Start from an issue: “fixes #123” in the PR description links the work.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. Find or create an issue and tell us you want to work on it.
  2. Fork FixMyMedTech/fixmymedtech-app (or add a remote to your own fork).
  3. Create a branch from dev, with a short descriptive name, e.g. fix/avatar-menu-stale-session.
  4. Make small, focused commits — one logical change per commit, with a clear message.
  5. Run the tests and linting before pushing (see docs/docs/setup.md).
  6. Open a Pull Request to dev describing what changed and referencing the issue.
  7. A maintainer reviews, you may be asked for tweaks, and then it is merged.

docs.title: PR checklist
docs.text:
• Code follows the project conventions (see docs/docs/architecture.md).
  • No secrets, credentials, or personal data added.
  • Backend changes include a migration in infrastructure/migrations/ when the schema changes.
  • Docs are updated when behaviour is user-visible.
  • Tests still pass.

docs.title: 3. Join the community
docs.text:
We coordinate on Discord — questions, ideas, bug triage and announcements happen there.

  • Join our Discord
  • Development and English/French/Spanish discussion welcome.

docs.title: 4. Contact us
docs.text:
• Project & deployments: fixmymedtech.org
  • Dev deployment: dev.fixmymedtech.org
  • Production deployments: platform.fixmymedtech.org

  • Email: email

  • GitHub: FixMyMedTech/fixmymedtech-app

Whether you are a biomedical engineer, a clinician, a developer, or someone who wants to see repairs happen in LMICs — we would love to hear from you.

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text:
All application tables live in a single PostgreSQL schema, fixmymedtech, and are created/updated by the ordered SQL files in infrastructure/migrations/, applied automatically at backend startup (tracked in fixmymedtech.schema_migrations).

Conventions

  • Every row uses a UUID primary key (default gen_random_uuid()), so IDs never collide across environments and are safe to use in public QR URLs.
  • Users vs. profiles: authentication identity lives in users (managed by FastAPI-Users, JWTs signed with AUTH_JWT_SECRET). Per-user profile data lives in profiles, whose id mirrors users.id 1:1.
  • Storage: photo/avatar/document binaries are stored in MinIO. The tables only keep the object key (e.g. profiles/<uuid>/avatar_<hex>.jpg).
  • Timestamps use TIMESTAMPTZ (timezone-aware).
erDiagram
    users ||--o| profiles : "1:1 (id)"
    organizations ||--o{ org_users : "has members"

docs.title: users
docs.text:
Local authentication identity (FastAPI-Users / password + JWT). Supabase's auth.users is not used.

Column Type Nullable Default Notes id UUID No (PK) gen_random_uuid() Shared 1:1 with profiles.id email TEXT No — UNIQUE; login identifier hashed_password TEXT Yes — bcrypt hash; empty for legacy/placeholder users is_active BOOLEAN No TRUE Disabled users cannot log in is_superuser BOOLEAN No FALSE Grants admin-portal access is_verified BOOLEAN No FALSE Set after email verification full_name TEXT Yes — Display name created_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW() updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW() Auto-updated on change

docs.title: profiles
docs.text:
Per-user profile data. One row per user; id = users.id.

Column Type Nullable Default Notes id UUID No (PK, FK) — FOREIGN KEY → users.id ON DELETE CASCADE username TEXT No — UNIQUE; used in URLs and UI full_name TEXT Yes — Display name (may mirror users.full_name) avatar_key TEXT Yes — MinIO key of the profile photo, e.g. profiles/<uuid>/avatar_<hex>.jpg country TEXT Yes — User-submitted country (registration/profile) created_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW()

docs.title: organizations
docs.text:
Hospitals, clinics, labs, etc. that own devices.

Column Type Nullable Default Notes id UUID No (PK) gen_random_uuid() name TEXT No — country TEXT No — region TEXT Yes — Region/province within country type TEXT Yes hospital CHECK in (hospital, clinic, health_centre, lab, engineering) contact_email TEXT Yes — created_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW() updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW() Auto-updated on change

docs.title: org_users
docs.text:
Junction table linking a profile to an organization with a role. A user can belong to several organizations with a different role in each.

Column Type Nullable Default Notes id UUID No (PK) gen_random_uuid() profile_id UUID No (FK) — FOREIGN KEY → profiles.id ON DELETE CASCADE organization_id UUID No (FK) — FOREIGN KEY → organizations.id ON DELETE CASCADE role TEXT No admin CHECK in (admin, technician, clinical_staff, engineering_staff) created_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW()

UNIQUE (profile_id, organization_id) — one role per user per org.

docs.title: device_categories
docs.text:
Device guide categories (pre-seeded by migration 010).

Column Type Nullable Default Notes id UUID No (PK) gen_random_uuid() name TEXT No — Display name slug TEXT No — UNIQUE; referenced by devices.category_id icon TEXT Yes 🏥 Emoji shown in lists

docs.title: devices
docs.text:
Medical equipment. All 20 pre-seeded categories exist from migration 010.

Column Type Nullable Default Notes id UUID No (PK) gen_random_uuid() Used in public QR URL /d/{id} organization_id UUID No (FK) — Owning org, FOREIGN KEY → organizations.id organization_maintenance_id UUID No (FK) — Org that maintains it, FOREIGN KEY → organizations.id category_id TEXT Yes (FK) — FOREIGN KEY → device_categories.slug name TEXT No — manufacturer TEXT Yes — model TEXT Yes — serial_number TEXT Yes — manufacture_year INT Yes — acquisition_date DATE Yes — acquisition_type TEXT Yes purchased CHECK in (purchased, donated, leased) location TEXT Yes — Free-form building/room latitude FLOAT Yes — longitude FLOAT Yes — photo_key TEXT Yes — MinIO key of the original photo photo_processed_key TEXT Yes — MinIO key of the processed (white-background) photo status TEXT Yes operational CHECK in (operational, maintenance, fault, decommissioned) registered_by UUID Yes (FK) — Profile that registered it, FOREIGN KEY → profiles.id last_maintenance DATE Yes — next_maintenance DATE Yes — Suggests follow-up notes TEXT Yes — created_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW() updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW() Auto-updated on change

docs.title: documents
docs.text:
Manuals, quick guides, videos, diagrams, checklists. Attached either to a device or to a category (library-level).

Column Type Nullable Default Notes id UUID No (PK) gen_random_uuid() device_id UUID Yes (FK) — FOREIGN KEY → devices.id ON DELETE CASCADE; device-specific doc category_id UUID Yes (FK) — FOREIGN KEY → device_categories.id; category-level doc title TEXT No — type TEXT No — CHECK in (manual, quick_guide, video, diagram, checklist) language TEXT Yes en url TEXT No — Where the file/asset lives size_kb INT Yes — created_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW()

Exactly one of device_id / category_id should be set.

docs.title: maintenance_logs
docs.text:
Preventive, corrective, or inspection records for a device.

Column Type Nullable Default Notes id UUID No (PK) gen_random_uuid() device_id UUID No (FK) — FOREIGN KEY → devices.id ON DELETE CASCADE performed_by UUID Yes (FK) — Profile that did the work, FOREIGN KEY → profiles.id assigned_to UUID Yes (FK) — Profile the task is assigned to, FOREIGN KEY → profiles.id performed_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW() type TEXT No — CHECK in (preventive, corrective, inspection) description TEXT Yes — parts_replaced TEXT Yes — cost_usd NUMERIC(10,2) Yes — next_due DATE Yes — Next scheduled maintenance status TEXT No open CHECK in (open, in_progress, closed)

docs.title: fault_reports
docs.text:
Fault reports, typically submitted by clinical staff (often anonymously via a public QR link).

Column Type Nullable Default Notes id UUID No (PK) gen_random_uuid() device_id UUID No (FK) — FOREIGN KEY → devices.id ON DELETE CASCADE reported_by UUID Yes (FK) — Profile that reported it, FOREIGN KEY → profiles.id; NULL for anonymous reporter_name TEXT Yes — Free-text name on anonymous reports assigned_to UUID Yes (FK) — Technician profile assigned, FOREIGN KEY → profiles.id reported_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes NOW() description TEXT No — severity TEXT Yes medium CHECK in (low, medium, high, critical) status TEXT Yes open CHECK in (open, assigned, in_progress, resolved) resolved_at TIMESTAMPTZ Yes — resolution_notes TEXT Yes —

docs.title: schema_migrations
docs.text:
Bookkeeping table used by the migration runner (backend/migrations.py) to run each SQL file exactly once, in filename order.

Column Type Nullable Default Notes name TEXT No (PK) — Migration filename, e.g. 016_profile_country.sql applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ No NOW() When it ran

docs.title: Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide walks through deploying FixMyMedTech from scratch: provisioning the server, configuring nginx, and setting up the GitHub Actions deployment workflows for both development and production environments.

docs.title: 1. Architecture overview
docs.text:
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  browser / QR scan ─────▶│  nginx (host, :80/:443)                    │
                          │                                            │
                          │   prod.fixmymedtech.org ─▶ 127.0.0.1:5001  │  frontend (FastHTML)
                          │   dev.fixmymedtech.org  ─▶ 127.0.0.1:5002  │  frontend (FastHTML)
                          │   qr.fixmymedtech.org   ─▶ 301 ─▶ dev.fixmymedtech.org
                          │                                            │
                          └────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                      │                │
                                      ▼                ▼
                              frontend container   backend container (FastAPI :8888)
                                      │                │
                                      └───── HTTP ─────┘
                                              │   │
                       Supabase Postgres ◀────┘   │   (DB only, fixmymedtech schema)
                                                  ▼
                                     minio container (internal minio:9000)
                                       volumes: minio-data (per environment)
  • The frontend (FastHTML) runs on port 5001 inside the container (fasthtml.serve() default) and talks to the backend over Docker's network.
  • The backend (FastAPI) runs on port 8888 inside the container.
  • The MinIO container serves every stored object (minio:9000 internally) and keeps its data in the named minio-data volume.
  • On the host, docker compose publishes the services only to 127.0.0.1, so nothing is exposed publicly except through nginx. MinIO is never exposed by nginx — the frontend proxies image routes (e.g. /profile/photo) to the backend, which reads MinIO on the internal network.
Env App dir Compose file Frontend (host) Backend (host) MinIO (host) Prod /opt/fixmymedtech docker-compose.yml 127.0.0.1:5001 127.0.0.1:8888 127.0.0.1:9000/9001 Dev /opt/fixmymedtech-dev docker-compose.dev.yml 127.0.0.1:5002 127.0.0.1:8889 127.0.0.1:9002/9003

MinIO on a shared server. Each environment runs its own MinIO container and its own minio-data volume, so dev and prod never share objects. Both backends reach MinIO as minio:9000 on their internal compose network; only the host-published ports differ (prod 9000/9001, dev 9002/9003) — they must stay different when both stacks run on the same host, otherwise the second one fails to bind its ports. The bucket name defaults to fixmymedtech (override with MINIO_BUCKET), scoped to each stack's own MinIO. Set MINIO_ROOT_USER / MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD once, before any upload (see Troubleshooting).

docs.title: 2. DNS records
docs.text:
Create A records pointing all three subdomains to your server IP (one record per hostname):

Hostname Type Value prod.fixmymedtech.org A dev.fixmymedtech.org A qr.fixmymedtech.org A

naming Note: nginx cannot redirect qr → dev if DNS does not resolve the domain to the server. Verify with dig qr.fixmymedtech.org.

docs.title: 3. Server setup (one time)
docs.text:
Tested on Ubuntu 22.04 (arm64).

sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

# Docker + compose plugin
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

# nginx + certbot
sudo apt install -y nginx certbot python3-certbot-nginx

# (optional) firewall — allow only SSH, 80, 443
sudo ufw allow OpenSSH
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
sudo ufw enable

# app directories used by the deploy workflows
sudo mkdir -p /opt/fixmymedtech /opt/fixmymedtech-dev

Log out and back in so the docker group takes effect, then confirm: docker run --rm hello-world.

docs.title: 4. nginx setup
docs.text:
The nginx config lives in the repo at infrastructure/nginx/nginx.conf and is not deployed automatically — copy it manually:

sudo cp infrastructure/nginx/nginx.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/fixmymedtech
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/fixmymedtech /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/fixmymedtech

The file contains four server blocks:

  1. prod.fixmymedtech.org → proxy to 127.0.0.1:5001 (SSL).
  2. qr.fixmymedtech.org on :80 → 301 https://dev.fixmymedtech.org$request_uri.
  3. qr.fixmymedtech.org on :443 (SSL) → same 301 redirect.
  4. dev.fixmymedtech.org → proxy to 127.0.0.1:5002 (SSL), plus Certbot's :80 → :443 redirect block.

Important — conflicting server names. If you previously had a qr block in /etc/nginx/sites-available/default (or another file), nginx loads the first one it finds and ignores the rest, so the redirect silently stops working. Remove the duplicate qr.fixmymedtech.org server blocks from default, keeping only the ones in fixmymedtech:

sudo grep -rn "qr.fixmymedtech.org" /etc/nginx/
# then edit /etc/nginx/sites-available/default and delete the qr blocks
sudo nginx -t

Issue certificates (must match the ssl_certificate paths in the config):

sudo certbot certonly --nginx -d prod.fixmymedtech.org
sudo certbot certonly --nginx -d dev.fixmymedtech.org
sudo certbot certonly --nginx -d qr.fixmymedtech.org

Check and reload:

sudo nginx -t          # expect NO "conflicting server name" warnings
sudo systemctl reload nginx

docs.title: 5. Supabase projects
docs.text:
Create two projects (one for dev, one for prod) at https://supabase.com.

Only PostgreSQL is used from Supabase:

  • Authentication runs against our own fixmymedtech.users table (FastAPI-Users + JWTs signed with AUTH_JWT_SECRET) — no Supabase Auth or GoTrue dependency.
  • File storage (avatars, device photos, documents) runs on MinIO, not Supabase Storage.

Setup:

  1. No manual schema step needed — the backend creates the fixmymedtech schema and applies every migration from infrastructure/migrations/*.sql at startup (tracked in fixmymedtech.schema_migrations).
  2. Project Settings → Database → Connection string → copy the URI (use the pooler for remote access, DATABASE_URL).

docs.title: 6. GitHub Actions secrets
docs.text:
In the repo Settings → Environments create two environments:

  • development — deployed from the dev branch.
  • production — deployed from the main branch.

Add these secrets per environment (replace *_ with DEV_ or PROD_):

Secret (required unless noted) Description *_DEPLOY_HOST / *_DEPLOY_USER SSH host and user *_DEPLOY_KEY SSH private key *_DEPLOY_PORT SSH port (defaults to 22 if unset) *_SUPABASE_DB_URI Postgres URI → DATABASE_URL *_FRONTEND_URL Public frontend URL, e.g. https://dev.fixmymedtech.org *_PUBLIC_API_URL Public backend URL — base for email verification links *_SESSION_SECRET Signs the frontend session cookies (random, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32) *_AUTH_JWT_SECRET Signs API JWTs (random long string) *_MINIO_ROOT_USER / *_MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD MinIO admin credentials (shared by backend + minio container) *_MINIO_BUCKET (optional) Bucket name (default fixmymedtech) *_SUPERUSER_EMAIL / *_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD / *_SUPERUSER_NAME (optional) Auto-created admin on first deploy *_MAIL_SERVER / *_MAIL_PORT / *_MAIL_USERNAME / *_MAIL_PASSWORD / *_MAIL_FROM / *_MAIL_FROM_NAME (optional) SMTP — verification & password-reset emails *_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / *_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET / *_GITHUB_* / *_DISCORD_* (optional) OAuth sign-in (disabled when absent) *_GEMINI_API_KEY / *_AUTO_PROCESS_PHOTO (optional) Photo white-background processing

Notes:

  • AUTH_JWT_SECRET and SESSION_SECRET are different secrets — one signs JWTs in the backend, the other signs session cookies in the frontend. Never leave them at their dev defaults in production.
  • OAuth and GEMINI_API_KEY map to empty values when the secret is absent, so leaving them unset simply disables the feature (no .env corruption).

Secrets are mapped by the workflows:

  • .github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml → DEV_* secrets, development env, app dir /opt/fixmymedtech-dev, uses docker-compose.dev.yml.
  • .github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml → PROD_* secrets, production env, app dir /opt/fixmymedtech, uses docker-compose.yml.

docs.title: 7. What a deploy does
docs.text:
Each workflow runs three steps on a GitHub runner:

  1. Write .env on the server (via SSH) — expands the secrets into /opt/fixmymedtech[-dev]/.env (used by docker compose). It contains the full set: DATABASE_URL, DB_SCHEMA, FRONTEND_URL, PUBLIC_API_URL, SESSION_SECRET, AUTH_JWT_SECRET, MINIO_* credentials + bucket, SUPERUSER_*, the SMTP MAIL_* block, and the optional OAuth / GEMINI_API_KEY entries. API_URL is fixed to http://backend:8888 (internal network).
  2. Copy the code (via scp) — backend, frontend, the compose file, and infrastructure (so migrations ship with the image).
  3. Build and deploy — docker compose up -d --build --remove-orphans. This also builds/starts the minio service; its minio-data volume survives redeploys, so previously uploaded objects are preserved.

At container startup, the backend runs backend/migrations.py, which applies any pending SQL migrations from infrastructure/migrations/ before serving traffic.

Superuser auto-creation: if SUPERUSER_EMAIL / SUPERUSER_PASSWORD are present in the server's .env, the backend also creates (or promotes) that admin right after migrations — no manual SSH step needed. The workflows already map these from DEV_SUPERUSER_* and PROD_SUPERUSER_* GitHub secrets (SUPERUSER_NAME sets the display name).

Email links: verification emails are built from PUBLIC_API_URL (set it to the public URL where the API is reachable, e.g. https://dev.fixmymedtech.org), and password-reset links from FRONTEND_URL.

docs.title: 8. Shipping a release
docs.text:
• Dev: push to dev → auto-deploys to /opt/fixmymedtech-dev.
  • Prod: push to main → auto-deploys to /opt/fixmymedtech.
  • Manual: both workflows support workflow_dispatch — run them from the Actions tab.

After a deploy, verify:

# on the server, per environment
cd /opt/fixmymedtech[-dev]
docker compose ps
curl -s http://localhost:8888/health   # backend (prod 8888, dev 8889)
curl -sI https://dev.fixmymedtech.org  # or prod.fixmymedtech.org
curl -sI https://qr.fixmymedtech.org   # expect a 301 to dev

docs.title: 9. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix conflicting server name "qr..." ignored Duplicate qr block in sites-available/default — remove it, keep only the one in fixmymedtech, nginx -t + reload. qr.fixmymedtech.org not redirecting DNS A record missing; or the listen 443; block lacks the ssl flag / options-ssl includes. Signup returns 400 Bad Request Check docker compose logs backend for the traceback; most often the email is already registered or the SMTP settings (MAIL_*) are missing/invalid. Migrations not applied docker compose logs backend | grep -i migration — migrations run on backend startup against DATABASE_URL. App up but browser shows cert warning Certbot cert does not cover the hostname — re-issue with certbot certonly --nginx -d <host>. Profile/device photo returns 404 The object is missing in MinIO. Verify the backend container can reach minio:9000 (docker compose logs backend | grep -i minio); if the minio-data volume was recreated (docker volume rm), all objects are gone — uploads must be redone. Uploads fail / AccessDenied on get MINIO_ROOT_USER/MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD changed after data was written, or they differ between backend and the minio container. They must be identical in both services and stable — set them once before the first upload. Verification emails link to http://localhost:8888 PUBLIC_API_URL is empty — set it to the public backend URL and redeploy. Backend crashes at startup with invalid literal for int() with base 10 MAIL_PORT is empty — keep it numeric (the deploy workflow defaults it to 587).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine + Compose V2)
  • Git
  • A Supabase project (free tier works) — or any PostgreSQL database
  • (Optional) Python 3.12 + uv / pip if you want to run services outside Docker

docs.title: 1. Clone and configure
docs.text:
git clone <repo-url> && cd fixmymedtech-app

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env and fill in:

Variable Where to find it DATABASE_URL Postgres connection string (Supabase pooler or local). postgresql+asyncpg://… DB_SCHEMA fixmymedtech (default) FRONTEND_URL http://localhost:8888 for local dev

docs.title: Optional (for OAuth / email)
docs.text:
# OAuth (leave blank to disable the buttons)
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=
GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=
GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=

# SMTP (leave MAIL_SERVER blank to log emails to console instead)
MAIL_SERVER=
MAIL_PORT=587
MAIL_USERNAME=
MAIL_PASSWORD=
MAIL_FROM=noreply@fixmymedtech.org

# JWT signing secret (change in production)
AUTH_JWT_SECRET=replace-with-a-random-string

docs.title: Option A — Local stack (PostgreSQL + MinIO, no account needed)
docs.text:
Recommended for day-to-day development. Runs the whole app against a local PostgreSQL container, no Supabase project required:

docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up --build -d

This builds and starts four containers:

Service URL What it does db localhost:5432 PostgreSQL 16 (isolated pg-data volume) minio console http://localhost:9003 S3-compatible file storage backend http://localhost:8888 FastAPI REST API frontend http://localhost:5001 FastHTML server-side UI

On first boot the database is initialised from infrastructure/db/init.sql, then the backend auto-applies every migration in infrastructure/migrations/ in order.

The local stack uses its own compose project (fixmymedtech-local), so its pg-data / minio-data volumes and host ports are independent of Option B below — switch between them freely without losing data.

docs.title: Option B — Supabase / remote PostgreSQL
docs.text:
If you prefer to develop against your Supabase project, set DATABASE_URL in .env (see section 1) and run:

docker compose up --build -d

This builds and starts two containers:

Service URL What it does backend http://localhost:8888 FastAPI REST API frontend http://localhost:5001 FastHTML server-side UI

Once running:

  • App: http://localhost:5001
  • API docs (Swagger): http://localhost:8888/docs
  • Admin portal: http://localhost:8888/admin/ (superuser only — see below)
  • MinIO console: http://localhost:9003 (Option A only — creds minioadmin/minioadmin)

docs.title: First-time setup — create a superuser
docs.text:
After the containers are up, create your first admin account:

docker compose exec backend python utils/create_superuser.py

(With the local stack, add -f docker-compose.local.yml: docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml exec backend python utils/create_superuser.py)

The script asks for email, name, and password interactively. It creates the user (with profile + default org) and marks them as superuser.

To promote an existing user to superuser, run the script with their email — it will update their password and grant superuser access.

Automated (recommended for servers/deploys): instead set SUPERUSER_EMAIL, SUPERUSER_PASSWORD (and optional SUPERUSER_NAME) in your environment — the backend then creates/promotes that admin automatically on every startup, right after applying migrations. The dev/prod deploy workflows already pass these through from the DEV_SUPERUSER_* / PROD_SUPERUSER_* GitHub secrets.

docs.title: Send invitations & verification emails
docs.text:
Once logged in as a superuser at /admin/:

Feature Where What it does Invite a user /admin-panel/invite Creates an account and sends a verification email with a link to set their password Resend verification User detail page → "Send Verification Email" button Re-sends the verification email to an unverified user Password reset User detail page → "Send Password Reset" button Sends a password reset link to the user

Note: When MAIL_SERVER is not configured (default for local dev), emails are logged to the backend console instead of being sent. Check docker compose logs backend to see the email content and verification links.

docs.title: 3. Project structure
docs.text:
fixmymedtech-app1/
├── backend/                          ← FastAPI REST API
│   ├── main.py                       ← App entry, CORS, router registration, SQLAdmin
│   ├── admin_auth.py                 ← SQLAdmin auth (superuser-only login)
│   ├── migrations.py                 ← Auto-runs SQL migration files on startup
│   ├── config/
│   │   ├── db_config.py               ← DB engine + async session factory
│   │   ├── users.py                  ← FastAPI-Users: UserManager, JWT backend, deps
│   │   ├── email.py                  ← fastapi-mail config (SMTP or console fallback)
│   │   └── oauth.py                  ← Authlib OAuth client (Google/GitHub)
│   ├── models/
│   │   └── models.py                 ← SQLAlchemy models (User, Profile, Device, …)
│   ├── routers/
│   │   ├── auth.py                   ← /api/auth/* (login, signup, me, tasks, …)
│   │   ├── oauth.py                  ← /api/auth/oauth/{provider} (social login)
│   │   ├── devices.py                ← /api/devices/*
│   │   ├── fault_reports.py          ← /api/faults/*
│   │   ├── maintenance_logs.py       ← /api/maintenance-logs/*
│   │   ├── dashboard.py              ← /api/dashboard/*
│   │   └── organizations.py          ← /api/organizations/*
│   ├── utils/
│   │   ├── profile.py                ← get_current_profile dependency
│   │   └── username.py               ← Auto-generate unique usernames
│   └── requirements.txt

docs.title: 5. Admin portal
docs.text:
The admin portal at /admin/ uses SQLAdmin to provide a browsable database UI.

Who can access: Only users with is_superuser = true in the fixmymedtech.users table.

Available models:

Model What it shows Users Auth accounts (email, is_active, is_verified, is_superuser) Profiles User profiles (username, full_name) Org Users User↔Organization links and roles Organizations Hospitals, clinics, etc. Device Categories Equipment categories (seeded from CSV) Devices All registered equipment Documents Manuals, guides, videos linked to devices Fault Reports Submitted fault reports Maintenance Logs Maintenance history

docs.title: 6. Database migrations
docs.text:
Migrations live in infrastructure/migrations/ and are named NNN_description.sql. They run automatically on backend startup in numeric order. Each migration is recorded in fixmymedtech.schema_migrations so it only runs once.

To add a new migration:

# Pick the next number
cat > infrastructure/migrations/013_my_change.sql << 'SQL'
ALTER TABLE fixmymedtech.devices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS warranty_end DATE;
SQL

Restart the backend container and it will apply automatically.

docs.title: Create a new API endpoint
docs.text:
1. Add your route in the relevant backend/routers/*.py file
  2. Use Depends(current_active_user) for auth, or Depends(get_current_profile) for profile + org context
  3. Register the router in backend/main.py if it's a new file

docs.title: Add a new database model
docs.text:
1. Define the model in backend/models/models.py
  2. Create a migration SQL in infrastructure/migrations/
  3. Add a ModelView in backend/main.py for the admin portal

docs.title: Run a one-off DB query
docs.text:
docker compose exec backend python -c "
import asyncio
from config.db_config import engine
from sqlalchemy import text

async def main():
    async with engine.begin() as conn:
        result = await conn.execute(text('SELECT count(*) FROM fixmymedtech.users'))
        print('Users:', result.scalar())

asyncio.run(main())
"

docs.title: 1. Supabase setup
docs.text:
1. Create a project at https://supabase.com
  2. The schema is applied automatically — backend startup runs the migrations in infrastructure/migrations/ (tracked in fixmymedtech.schema_migrations).
  3. Go to Project Settings → API → copy:
  4. Project URL
  5. anon public key
  6. service_role secret key

docs.title: 2. Backend setup
docs.text:
cd backend
cp .env.example .env
# Fill in DATABASE_URL (and DB_SCHEMA)

pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn main:app --reload
# API runs at http://localhost:8000
# Docs at http://localhost:8000/docs

docs.title: 3. Frontend setup
docs.text:
cd frontend
cp .env.example .env
# Set PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000

npm install
npm run dev
# Runs at http://localhost:5173

docs.title: Offline behaviour (PWA) - Nice to have
docs.text:
• Device pages (/d/{id}) are cached by the Service Worker after first visit
  • Manuals/PDFs cached for 30 days
  • API responses cached for 7 days
  • Fault reports require internet connection to submit
